paragraphs.text: Craft is turning into a linter.
said it plainly this week: he hasn’t seen a project with obvious design mistakes in a while. AI raised the floor, and a decent-looking design is now just the baseline.
The rules that got us here are being written down. Emil shipped
that handles stagger and timing when several things animate together.
just passed 20,000 design reviews, and most came from agents checking UI while they write it. The rules are small and geometric: inner radius equals outer radius minus padding, and
I think that’s mostly great. Müller-Brockmann wrote his grid down for the same reason. But

spotted the catch: left alone, models add documentation instead of simplifying. A linter can tell you a corner is wrong. Knowing the screen shouldn’t exist takes context, and context is the next thing agents get.
The corners are solved. The question now is who supplies the context.
